questions.prompt: A class in another assembly derives from your class. Which access modifier lets that derived class use a member of yours?
options: `internal`
`private protected`
`protected internal`
`file`
questions.explanation: `protected internal` allows access within the same assembly or from derived classes, even in different assemblies. `private protected` limits derived access to the same assembly, and `internal` has no derived-class exception.

source.section: `protected internal` - Accessible from assembly or derived types

questions.prompt: Where can a `readonly` field be assigned?
options: Anywhere inside the class, but not from outside it
Only at the point of declaration or inside the constructor
Only inside static methods
Nowhere; it must be a compile-time constant like `const`
questions.explanation: A `readonly` field can only be assigned at its declaration or in the constructor of its class or struct; assigning it in another method such as `UpdateYear` is an error.

source.section: `readonly` - Field is assigned only during declaration

questions.prompt: With `int a = int.MaxValue;`, what happens to `int b = a + 1;` inside a `checked` block compared with an `unchecked` block?
options: `checked` wraps to `int.MinValue`; `unchecked` throws an `OverflowException`
Both blocks throw an `OverflowException`
Both blocks silently keep `int.MaxValue`
`checked` throws an `OverflowException`; `unchecked` wraps to `int.MinValue`
questions.explanation: `checked` enables overflow detection and throws `OverflowException`; `unchecked` suppresses it, so the value wraps to `int.MinValue` (-2147483648).

questions.prompt: Given `object obj = 42;`, what is the difference between `(string)obj` and `obj as string`?
options: `(string)obj` throws an `InvalidCastException`; `obj as string` gives `null` without an exception
Both return `"42"`
`(string)obj` returns `null`; `obj as string` throws an `InvalidCastException`
Both throw an `InvalidCastException`
questions.explanation: `as` is a safe cast that returns `null` when the cast fails, while a direct cast throws `InvalidCastException`.

source.section: `as` - Safe cast; returns null if incompatible

questions.prompt: When should a custom conversion operator be declared `explicit` instead of `implicit`?
options: When the conversion is safe, lossless and unsurprising
When the conversion may lose information, fail, or is not obvious to the caller
When the conversion operator is not `public static`
When neither side of the conversion is the containing type
questions.explanation: `explicit` makes the caller write a cast, so the conversion is visible; the note says to use it when the conversion may lose information, fail, or is not obvious. Safe, lossless conversions can be `implicit`.
